description: Use this when the user wants a scannable QR code woven into a picture they already have (a photo, an illustration or artwork) instead of one painted from a description. Pass the picture once, as exactly one of an attached file (image), a public https link (imageUrl) or base64 (imageBase64): PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 10 MB and at least 256 pixels on each side; the code uses its centre square. Every picture is checked for safety first, and one that does not pass is refused with an error and nothing is made. It starts the code and answers at once with its id while it is painted, which usually takes under a minute; then call get_qr_code with the id to wait for the image. Do not use it to look at, list or change codes that already exist. Each code counts against the user’s QRX allowance.

destination.description: The link scans open: an absolute http or https URL, e.g. https://example.com/menu.

image.description: The picture as a file the user attached in the conversation.

download_url.description: Where the file can be downloaded.

imageBase64.description: Or: the picture as base64, or a base64 data: URL.

imageUrl.description: Or: a public https link to the picture.

prompt.description: Optional: what the picture shows, to guide how it is redrawn. Leave out to have it described automatically.

style.description: A style id from list_styles. Leave out to keep the picture’s own look.

name: generate_qr_code_from_image
